extracted.intended_audience: users (new and existing) of Mathematics Stack Exchange
extracted.subtask_description: The site Help Center for Mathematics Stack Exchange listing site rules, FAQs, and guidance for asking, answering, moderation, reputation, formatting, and account issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take the 2-minute tour
rubrics_metrics.description: New to Mathematics Stack Exchange? Find out everything you need to get started by taking the tour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduction to how the site works and recommended first steps for new users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anybody can ask
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone may post a question on the site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the site's operating model; invites users to ask questions subject to topicality and quality guidance available in the help center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anybody can answer
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone may post answers to questions on the site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the site's operating model; answers are community-contributed and subject to voting and moderation.

rubrics_metrics.name: The best answers are voted up and rise to the top
rubrics_metrics.description: Answers are ranked by community votes so that the most useful answers become most visible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voting is the primary mechanism for surface high-quality content.

rubrics_metrics.name: What topics can I ask about here?
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on which mathematical topics and question types are appropriate for Mathematics Stack Exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the topical scope of the site and what constitutes an on-topic question versus off-topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: What types of questions should I avoid asking?
rubrics_metrics.description: List of question styles and content that are discouraged or off-topic for the site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically covers overly broad questions, opinion-based questions, homework dumps without effort, and questions lacking necessary detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: What does it mean if a question is "closed" or "on hold"?
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanation of the closed/on-hold state applied to questions and the reasons for closure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes closure reasons (duplicate, off-topic, unclear, too broad, opinion-based) and the implications for editing and reopening.

rubrics_metrics.name: What if I disagree with the closure of a question? How can I reopen it?
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and steps for disputing a closure and getting a question reopened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains editing to address issues, voting to reopen, and use of Meta or flags to seek moderator attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why and how are some questions deleted?
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasons and processes by which questions may be deleted from the site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers community deletion, moderator deletion, automatic removal criteria, and the permanent effects of deletion.

rubrics_metrics.name: What kind of behavior is expected of users?
rubrics_metrics.description: Code of conduct and behavioral expectations for participation on the site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes civility, respect, avoiding harassment, and following site norms for constructive Q&A.

rubrics_metrics.name: How do I find topics I'm interested in?
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on locating questions and tags that match a user's interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains use of tags, search, favorite tags, and browsing features.

rubrics_metrics.name: How do I search?
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for using the site's search functionality effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include search syntax, filters, and tips for finding existing questions/answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: How do I format my posts using Markdown or HTML?
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions on formatting questions and answers using Markdown (and limited HTML) for readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers code/math formatting, lists, headings, inline math (where applicable), and general presentation tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: What is "meta"? How does it work?
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanation of the Meta site and how to use it for discussion about site policies and community decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes when to post on Meta vs. the main site, how to ask policy or feature questions, and community governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: What is a bounty? How can I start one?
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about reputation bounties: what they are and the process for offering them to attract attention to a question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains costs, minimum/maximum amounts, eligibility, and effects on visibility and answer selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: What is reputation? How do I earn (and lose) it?
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanation of the reputation system as a measure of community trust and how actions affect reputation points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details points for votes, accepted answers, bounties, association bonuses, and reputation losses (downvotes, bounties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who are the site moderators, and what is their role here?
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of moderator responsibilities and how they help maintain site quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains elected moderators' powers, community moderation, and how to contact moderators or flag content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why is voting important?
rubrics_metrics.description: Rationale for the voting system and its role in surfacing quality content and moderating the site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages voting as a core community activity that rewards helpful posts and guides content visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: What does it mean when an answer is "accepted"?
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanation of the accepted-answer mechanism and what acceptance signifies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that acceptance is the asker's selection of the answer they found most helpful and its effect on reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to reference material written by others
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on properly citing and attributing external sources used in posts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers quoting, attribution, plagiarism avoidance, and providing links to sources for verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why and how are some answers deleted?
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasons answers may be removed and the mechanisms for deletion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes community deletion, moderator actions, low-quality/abusive content policies, and consequences for repeat offenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why are answers no longer being accepted from my account?
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanation of account-level restrictions that can prevent posting answers (e.g., bans).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes quality bans, causes (poor-post history), and steps to improve to regain posting privileges.

rubrics_metrics.name: How do I write a good answer?
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on composing helpful, well-explained answers that solve the asker's problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically recommends showing work, providing explanation/intuition, being concise but complete, using proper formatting, and avoiding one-line/low-effort posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: View a full list of badges you can earn
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference list of site badges and the criteria to earn them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displays bronze/silver/gold badges with brief descriptions of the actions required to obtain each.

rubrics_metrics.name: View a full list of privileges you can earn
rubrics_metrics.description: List of site privileges unlocked at various reputation thresholds and what each privilege allows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows reputation requirements and descriptions for actions like commenting, voting, flagging, reviewing, and moderation tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: I lost my password; how do I reset it?
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for recovering access to an account when the password is lost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically includes using the 'forgot password' flow, email verification, and account recovery options.

rubrics_metrics.name: How do I delete my account?
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure and implications for permanently deleting a user account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the deletion request process, effects on content and reputation, and the possibility of account removal delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why has my post been blocked due to 'spam and abuse from my network'?
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanation of network-level blocks that may prevent posting due to suspected spam/abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes common triggers, steps to resolve, and how to contact support if blocked in error.

rubrics_metrics.name: How do I report a possible security vulnerability?
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for responsibly reporting security issues found on the site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides contact channels and guidance on what information to include while avoiding public disclosure of exploit details.

rubrics_metrics.name: I accidentally created two accounts; how do I merge them?
rubrics_metrics.description: Process for merging duplicate user accounts and the requirements for verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how to request a merge and the consequences for reputation, posts, and associated logins.
